decisions.reason: As a component that builds directly on the established radiant-heating business, it is cheap to carry and worth keeping while market acceptance and retrofit demand continue to resolve.
The electric infrared panel heater fits the firm's lower-carbon direction, so management would likely keep this option open despite some overlap with other new electric offerings.
The electric halogen infrared heater looks more peripheral and substitutable within a crowded new-product set, so if early evidence stays limited the firm is likely to reallocate resources elsewhere.
This industrial electric infrared hall heater is close to the core offer for halls and workshops, making it a strategically relevant option whose uncertainty still justifies staying in the market.

The hydrogen-capable gas dark infrared heater is strongly aligned with the firm's stated move toward hydrogen-ready low-carbon systems and already has an early operating reference, so management would be inclined to retain it.
